newsitem.title: RWANDA: Three Spanish aid workers, 3 Rwandans murdered.
newsitem.headline: Three Spanish aid workers, 3 Rwandans murdered.

text.p: Rwandan Hutu militiamen shot dead three Spanish aid workers and three soldiers and seriously wounded an American in an overnight attack in northwestern Rwanda, survivors said.
Bodies of the three Spaniards -- two men and a woman -- lay in pools of blood in the aid workers' house when a Reuters correspondent reached Ruhengeri on Sunday.
"These people were executed. Clearly these attacks were aimed at aid workers and expatriates generally," United Nations Human Rights Operation director Javier Zuniga told Reuters.

The American, named by aid workers as Nitin Madhav, was working with the Spaniards. He was treated in the local hospital at Ruhengeri, where his wounded leg was amputated, and later was flown to Kigali and evacuated for further treatment.

An American diplomat said the attackers stormed into the house and demanded the Spaniards' passports. They were then disturbed by the noise of gunfire outside the house, and reacted by shooting the three from close range.
Madhav, aged 28 and from the Pittsburgh area of Pennyslvania, was shot in the leg as he dived behind a table in a bid to escape the attackers' bullets.

The Spaniards, shot through the head, were attached to the Spanish charity Medicos del Mundo (Doctors of the World). In Paris the parent group Medecins du Monde announced that it was suspending all activities in Rwanda pending further information about the killings.

In Madrid, Medicos del Mundo named the dead as doctor Manuel Madrazo, 42, from Seville, nurse Maria Flors Sirera, 33, from Lerida, and Luis Valtuena, 30, a photographer from Madrid who was working as an administrator in Rwanda.
Most expatriate staff in the Ruhengeri area left for the capital Kigali where the United Nations, international relief groups and the government will hold a crisis meeting on Monday.
That meeting will decide whether to formally suspend humanitarian work in parts of Rwanda on security grounds.
"Most of the expatriate in Ruhengeri have already reached Kigali. The mood is very sombre," a Western diplomat said.
Spain condemned the murder of its three nationals and advised its citizens in the region to leave as soon as possible.

"We condemn the killings and have sent condolences to the families and now we are concentrating on getting the corpses back and advising those still there to leave," Foreign Ministry spokesman Inocencio Arias said in Madrid.
A senior Rwandan military officer told Reuters: "These attacks are deliberately mounted to scare away expatriates."
"U.N. people have been told to stay put and not go out. And as soon as we have talked to the army we will be discussing whether or not to suspend operations," a U.N. official said.

"The fighting appeared to have started in the slum areas of town among returnees who have come back from Zaire. There were two other incidents during the night during which a grenade was thrown into an aid worker's house," a senior U.N. official said.
The attack was the latest in a series involving expatriates in the area, which is near the border with Zaire.
The house was in a compound housing Medicos del Mundo, Medecins du Monde and Save the Children 225 km (140-miles) northwest of the capital, Kigali.
The three Rwandan soldiers were killed in the attack on the Spaniards' house, aid workers said.

A Rwandan military officer said: "We know these people are now operating from inside Rwanda. They think if they can drive out the expatriates now working here they can mount such attacks He said the gangs responsible for recent attacks on aid workers had returned from neighbouring Zaire with other Rwandan refugees late last year. They were now becoming bolder, he said.
The United Nations had warned on Saturday that escalating violence in Rwanda could force the suspension of humanitarian operations in some areas.

Hardline Hutu militiamen, troops and mobs killed an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus in Rwanda in 1994. Many of the militiamen fled to neighbouring countries after Tutsi rebels seized power and ended the three-month genocide.
